## Definition

A finite-dimensional complex matrix input of dimension $d$ is **effectively encoded** if its complete binary description specifies $d$ and conforms to one fixed deterministic entry-approximation machine. Given the description, an entry index, and unary precision request $1^p$, that machine returns rational real and imaginary parts within $2^{-p}$ of the exact entry in time bounded by one fixed polynomial in the total description length plus $p$, uniformly over all valid encodings. Rational entries use their exact binary numerator and denominator; algebraic entries use a finite encoding compatible with this same evaluator and bound. A **uniform matrix family** supplies one polynomial-time description-generation procedure for each member. Hermiticity, dimensions, and norm bounds are promises on the exact matrices, not conclusions inferred from a finite approximation.

This interface includes finite output size and all approximation bit costs. It does not supply a matrix oracle, exact comparisons on arbitrary computable reals, or a free unitary implementation.

## Statement

For each integer $d\ge1$, the degree-$d$ Bernstein polynomial
$$B_d(x)=\sum_{j=0}^d\sqrt{j/d}\binom djx^j(1-x)^{d-j}$$
satisfies $\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|B_d(x)-\sqrt{x}|\le(4d)^{-1/4}$. Consequently degree $d\ge1/(4\eta^4)$ suffices for uniform error at most $\eta>0$.

## Statement

Let $U$ be unitary on a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $M$ be an endomorphism with $\|M-U\|\le\varepsilon\le1/8$. Then $M$ is invertible and its polar unitary $Q=M(M^*M)^{-1/2}$ satisfies $\|Q-U\|\le2\varepsilon$. The inverse square root is defined by the positive spectral square root. When $M$ has effectively computable entries in fixed dimension, the inverse square root also has an effective matrix approximation: expand $(I+X)^{-1/2}$ at $X=M^*M-I$, whose norm is less than $1/2$, and truncate the absolutely convergent binomial series.

## Statement

Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $S\subseteq H$ be a nonzero subspace. Let $H_1,H_2$ be Hermitian endomorphisms, with $H_2|_S=0$ and $\langle H_2v,v\rangle\ge J\|v\|^2$ for every $v\in S^\perp$, where $J>2\|H_1\|$. Write $\lambda_S=\lambda_{\min}(H_1|_S)$. Then

$$\lambda_S-\frac{\|H_1\|^2}{J-2\|H_1\|}\le\lambda_{\min}(H_1+H_2)\le\lambda_S.$$

Here $H_1|_S$ is the compression $P_SH_1P_S$ on $S$, where $P_S$ is orthogonal projection. Assume $S\ne\{0\}$ so that $\lambda_S$ is defined. If $S^\perp=\{0\}$, the lower spectral hypothesis is vacuous and the conclusion reduces to equality.

## Statement

Use the exact one-qubit matrices $H$ and $T=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\pi/4})$ of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]]. The matrices $h=iH$ and $t=e^{-i\pi/8}T$, together with their inverses, are determinant-one representatives in $SU(2)$. Their generated subgroup is dense in $SU(2)$. Replacing each normalized letter in a word by its underlying physical $H,T,T^\dagger$ letter changes the product only by one scalar phase, so an unconditional one-qubit circuit can approximate every $SU(2)$ target up to an irrelevant global phase. A normalized letter must not be placed under a control without correcting its scalar phase.

## Definition

Fix an integer $k\ge1$. An encoded instance of input length $N$ gives $n,m\ge1$, with $n$ polynomially bounded in $N$ and $m$ polynomially bounded in $n$, and explicitly lists a finite matrix description for each Hermitian $H_j$ and its support on at most $k$ of the $n$ qubits. It also gives a positive rational polynomial bound $B$ with $\|H_j\|\le B$ for every exact term. Matrix descriptions and their approximation procedures use [[def-qa-33-effective-finite-matrix-encoding]]. Embed each local matrix by identity on unlisted qubits and put $H=\sum_{j=1}^m H_j$ on $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}$. Given rational thresholds $a<b$ with $b-a\ge1/p(n)$ for a polynomial $p$, the promise problem has YES instances when $\lambda_{\min}(H)\le a$ and NO instances when $\lambda_{\min}(H)\ge b$. Inputs violating the format or promise are outside the promise; no behavior is required there. A matrix description is not a free measurement oracle: a verifier must generate every local test circuit from the finite encoding.

## Definition

For an input length $n$, let $X_n=\mathcal Q_n$ be the ordered classical-input register, $W_n=\mathcal Q_{w(n)}$ a witness register, and $A_n=\mathcal Q_{a(n)}$ a clean-ancilla register; $w(n),a(n)$ are polynomially bounded and zero qubits means the one-dimensional space $\mathbb C$. A verifier family is one full-list uniform family of finite circuits on $X_n\otimes W_n\otimes A_n$, generated in polynomial time from $1^n$. Its gate order and unitary denotation are those of [[def-qc-uniform-circuit-family]], [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]], and [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. The first register holds the classical basis input $|x\rangle$, the witness may be any density operator $\rho$ on $W_n$, and the clean ancillas start in $|0^{a(n)}\rangle$. Thus this definition adds an explicit quantum witness register to the classical-input, zero-ancilla promise-computation convention of [[def-qc-promise-computation-model]]; a witness is not an initialized ancilla.

Let $O_n$ be the ordered tuple of distinct terminally measured wires. A total polynomial-time predicate $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,z)$ determines acceptance from the measured output string $z$. Let $J_x:W_n\to X_n\otimes W_n\otimes A_n$ be $J_x\psi=|x\rangle\otimes\psi\otimes|0^{a(n)}\rangle$, and let $P_x$ be the orthogonal projection onto all computational-basis output strings accepted by $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,\cdot)$, tensored with the identity on every unmeasured wire. Define the witness acceptance effect and its probability by

$$E_x:=J_x^*U_n^*P_xU_nJ_x,\qquad p_V(x,\rho):=\operatorname{Tr}(E_x\rho).$$

The projection $P_x$ sums over every unmeasured output wire. The positivity of this compression and its equality with the terminal outcome law are proved separately. The matrix input, gate list, generator, output predicate, and all circuit and classical costs are charged according to [[def-qc-circuit-cost-model]]; no intermediate measurement or free random source is assumed in this base interface.

## Statement

Fix a nonnegative integer $q$ and dimension $D=2^q$, independent of input length. Given a $D\times D$ unitary whose entries have polynomial-time Cauchy names from a finite description and a rational $0<\eta<1/2$, a deterministic polynomial-time procedure outputs a circuit on its $q$ data wires, with a constant number of clean ancillas returned to zero, for which there is a unit scalar $\lambda$ with $\|V-\lambda U\|\le\eta$. The procedure has polynomial bit cost and polynomial gate count in the description length and $1/\eta$. Scalar phase is immaterial only for this unconditional circuit. The construction uses complex Givens elimination with robust pivoting, a constant-width decomposition into unconditional one-qubit $SU(2)$ rotations and CNOT gates, and the finite-precision compiler of [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity]]. Its exact reversible-control subconstruction gives Toffoli from $H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}$ by the parity-phase identity in the proof.

Fix $k$ and let $H=\sum_{j=1}^mH_j$ be an encoded $k$-local Hamiltonian with $m=\operatorname{poly}(n)$, local dimension at most $D=2^k$, and algebraic entries supplied by polynomial-time Cauchy procedures. For every rational $\tau>0$, a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm outputs rational Hermitian local matrices $\widetilde H_j$ with $\sum_j\|H_j-\widetilde H_j\|\le\tau$. A concrete polynomial running-time conclusion requires the stated polynomial-time Cauchy bounds for each algebraic entry encoding.

Fix $k$. Let $K$ be a Hermitian matrix on at most $k$ qubits with rational or effectively encoded algebraic entries of bit length $b$, let $B\ge\|K\|$ be a positive rational of bit length $b$, and set $E=(I-K/B)/2$. For any rational $0<\eta<1/2$, a deterministic polynomial-time generator in $b+\log B+1/\eta$ outputs a finite QC14 circuit with one flag bit whose measured outcome $1$ has effect $\widetilde E$ satisfying $\|\widetilde E-E\|\le\eta$. Let $U_0$ be the Naimark block unitary of the proof and define $U_{acc}=(X_{flag}\otimes I)U_0$. The construction supplies polynomial-time Cauchy names for $U_{acc}$ and a standalone dilation circuit whose unitary is within $\eta/2$, up to global phase, of $U_{acc}$. With one selector bit, [[lem-qa-33-finite-dimensional-unitary-synthesis]] compiles the full block diagonal matrix $I\oplus U_{acc}$ from those Cauchy names. Circuit size and generator bit time are polynomial in $b+\log B+1/\eta$. No local matrix is treated as a free gate or oracle.

## Statement

Use the fixed QC14 alphabet $\{H,T,T^\dagger,\mathrm{CNOT}\}$. Let $M$ be one fixed deterministic polynomial-time classical machine that, on each binary input $x$ of length $n$, outputs a valid circuit description $P_x$ of at most $L(n)$ gate records on at most $W(n)$ data wires, where $L,W$ are fixed polynomials. Encode the output as exactly $L(n)$ fixed-width records: each record is either blank, a one-qubit label $H,T,T^\dagger$ with one wire address, or a CNOT label with an ordered pair of distinct wire addresses; unused address fields are zero. Let $\delta(n)$ be any inverse-polynomial rational tolerance produced by a fixed polynomial-time machine from $1^n$, with polynomial bit length. There is a full-list uniform QC14 family generated from $1^n$ which on classical basis input $x$ and data state $|\psi\rangle$ outputs a state within operator error $\delta(n)$, up to a global scalar, of
$$|x\rangle\otimes P_x|\psi\rangle\otimes|M(x)\rangle\otimes|0^w\rangle$$
for a polynomially bounded work width $w(n)$. Its size and generator time are polynomial in $n$ and $1/\delta(n)$. The program and arithmetic registers are terminal unmeasured wires; their presence changes the data-register outcome law from executing $P_x$ by at most $2\delta(n)$. This lemma converts a polynomial-time input-dependent compiler into the input-length-uniform verifier model.

## Definition

Given a verifier for thresholds $0\le s<c\le1$, an integer $r\ge1$, and an $r$-copy witness register, partition the witness into $r$ blocks of the original witness length and give each copy of the verifier its own fresh clean ancillas and output bit. Run the $r$ finite verifier circuits on disjoint blocks, measure their terminal accept bits, and let $S$ be their sum. Accept exactly when

$$S\ge\left\lceil\frac{r(c+s)}2\right\rceil.$$

The rational midpoint and integer threshold are computed exactly from the binary encodings of $c,s,r$. For an arbitrary initial joint witness, including one entangled across the $r$ blocks, the verifier evaluates the same finite product circuit; soundness for this case is established in the separate proof of the entangled-witness amplification result.

## Definition

**Inputs:** A length-$n$ verifier from [[def-qa-33-witness-verifier-interface]], its classical basis input $|x\rangle$ with $|x|=n$, an $r$-block witness register, rational thresholds $0\le s<c\le1$, and an integer $r\ge1$. Each verifier has input register $X_n$, witness register $W_n$, clean ancillas $A_n$, terminally measured tuple $O_n$, and total predicate $\operatorname{Acc}_n(x,z)$. The admissible parameters are those of the verifier's promise-class contract, with $r$ polynomially bounded when polynomial resources are claimed.

**Procedure:** Partition the witness into $r$ blocks $W^{(1)},\ldots,W^{(r)}$. Use the given input register as $X^{(1)}$, allocate $r-1$ fresh zero-initialized $n$-bit registers $X^{(2)},\ldots,X^{(r)}$, and for every bit position $i$ and $j=2,\ldots,r$, apply a CNOT from $X^{(1)}_i$ to $X^{(j)}_i$. Since $x$ is a computational-basis string, this copies $|x\rangle$ exactly and leaves every input register in $|x\rangle$. Give each verifier copy its own fresh clean ancillas and distinct output wires, then run its finite circuit on $(X^{(j)},W^{(j)},A^{(j)})$. $$H'=\frac1{2L}\sum_{l,i}(|\eta_{l-1,i}\rangle-|\eta_{l,i}\rangle)(\langle\eta_{l-1,i}|-\langle\eta_{l,i}|).$$
